title: Your TA Company Is Trapped in a Browser Tab. Time to Let Them Out (part 4 of 6)
author: howtoteachwithai
source: How to Teach With AI (howtoteachwithai.substack.com), August 11, 2026
summary: Part four of a six-part series, the piece is a step-by-step guide for teachers to use Claude's 'Cowork' desktop mode to grade written student work directly on their own computer, eliminating the copy-paste cycle of pasting student reflections into a browser chat window and pasting feedback back into an LMS. The author walks through five concrete steps -- installing the desktop app and granting folder-limited file access, building a specific folder structure, seeding the Voice folder with real (not polished) past feedback samples to avoid generic-sounding AI output, writing a detailed grading-instruction template, and running the tool on one submission first as a 'calibration shot' before batch-processing a full class. Central to the pitch is a claim about what actually eats teacher time: 'A full third of grading time is admin work around the actual grading,' so Cowork's value isn't replacing the teacher's judgment but eliminating the tab-switching, copying, and formatting labor around it. The piece ends with named failure modes teachers commonly hit and specific instruction fixes for each, framed as troubleshooting rather than theory.
points: Provides a concrete, replicable folder architecture (Rubric / Voice / Submissions / Feedback) designed so an AI desktop assistant can navigate grading materials without teachers manually copying files into a chat window each time.

Identifies the specific failure mode of 'voice samples' that are too polished -- teachers default to pasting finished feedback letters, which trains the AI on institutional voice rather than the teacher's real, casual tone.

Builds in a mandatory calibration step ('Do not batch-grade until I sign off on the first one') explicitly because most teachers skip it and let the tool grade 22 submissions the same broken way before catching an error.

Frames the tool's value proposition narrowly and specifically -- eliminating admin overhead around grading, not replacing the teacher's judgment -- citing the claim that 'a full third of grading time is admin work around the actual grading.'
quotes: That is not grading. That is data entry in a nicer outfit. Cowork ends that.
A full third of grading time is admin work around the actual grading. Opening tabs. Copying. Pasting. Formatting. Saving to the right folder. Uploading to the LMS.
Grant file access only to the folder you're about to use for grading. Not your whole drive. You don't need Cowork reading your taxes.
Those three items train the Desktop Assistant in your voice faster than any prompt. Samples beat descriptions every time.
Most teachers skip this and tell Cowork to grade everything in one go. Don't. The first feedback letter is your calibration shot.
If the feedback was too generic, add this line to RULES. If the same feedback could apply to two different students, it fails. Rewrite with specific quotes from the submission.
